chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from al-Fadl ibn Zakariyya, from Najm ibn Hutm, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If people knew what is in the Mosque of Kufah, they would prepare for it provisions and a mount from a distant place. And he said: An obligatory prayer in it equals one Hajj, and a recommended prayer in it equals one 'Umrah.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying in the Mosque of Kufah according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) in *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the unique spiritual status of the Mosque of Kufah, historically linked to the martyrdom of Imam Ali (AS) and the early Islamic community. The equivalence of one obligatory prayer to a full Hajj and a voluntary prayer to an Umrah highlights the mosque's role as a focal point for both ritual devotion and historical remembrance in Shia tradition. This immense reward encourages believers to prioritize visiting and praying here, viewing it as a means of drawing closer to the Ahl al-Bayt.
